leah: Quick follow-up from today's design sync. I want to propose a sealed-claim token pattern to keep runtime checks tiny while preserving rich audit and revocation. Idea: short token carries subject, scope, and a `seal_id` (digest) that points to a signed claim blob stored in control plane (or CDN). Data plane validates signature of the claim issuer and compares local digest -> O(1).

oscar: Sounds promising. How does it differ from a big JWT with all claims embedded?

leah: Two differences: 1) the heavyweight metadata (role projections, partner proofs) stays server-side signed and versioned, so tokens are compact; 2) revocation is cheap: bump the sealed blob version or mark seal_id revoked and runtime sees mismatch.

mina: Walk me through runtime flow and failure modes.

leah: Runtime flow: 1) request carries Authorization: Bearer <compact> and x-rdwd-seal: <seal_id>. 2) service verifies compact signature and scope, then checks local cache for seal_id -> either cached signed blob or revocation marker. 3) If cache miss, fetch signed blob from control plane (async refresh) and proceed. Failure modes: stale cache (we treat as miss and fetch), control-plane outage (fail-open? prefer fail-closed for admin routes).

oscar: What about latency? fetch-on-miss could be slow on first calls.

leah: Mitigations: 1) aggressive caching (seal metadata small), 2) prefetching in gateway for known subjects, 3) allow services to accept a short grace TTL for seal mismatch (report but allow) during rollout windows. Goal: <1ms median added time for cache hits.

mina: Revocation model?

leah: Two-tier: short TTL on tokens (5-15m) for most use-cases + seal generation increments for emergency revokes. To revoke immediately, control plane increments seal generation or creates a revocation record keyed by seal_id; runtime checks cached generation number.

oscar: How do we handle delegation (service acting on behalf of user)?

leah: Broker issues a one-use sealed claim that includes an `on_behalf_of` field and a nonce. The broker stores nonce as single-use. The sealed blob ties the nonce -> runtime checks nonce usage via a small replay cache or control-plane lookup. Single-use tokens avoid long-lived impersonation windows.

mina: Migration from existing API keys?

leah: Phased: 1) keep existing keys working. 2) console surfaces suggestion to rotate long-lived keys to sealed claims and provides a tool to mint sealed blobs. 3) 10% traffic enforcement behind header gating (x-rdwd-seal required for opt-in routes). 4) 90-day deprecation window for legacy keys on partner routes.

oscar: Any security concerns? KMS for signing sealed blobs, protect blob storage, rate-limit fetch endpoints, and prevent armor by disallowing wildcard admin claims in sealed blobs unless manual approval. Also ensure seals are revocation-friendly so stolen tokens can't be used long.

mina: Telemetry and audit: log seal_id, subject, minting actor, and generation. Track seal cache hit-rate, miss latency, revocations, and delegation events. Retain mint events 1 year for partners.

leah: Action items:
- @oscar: prototype validator lib with cache + seal fetch (ETA 2w)
- @mina: write migration UX + console prompts (ETA 1w)
- @leah: draft short RFC with token shapes, fetch endpoint contract, and threat model (ETA 5d)
